title: Tap a beer keg with a Sankey D coupler
instruction: Tap the keg with the coupler.
context: Changing kegs is routine bar work: the coupler goes onto the keg's Sankey valve, turns a quarter turn under the valve's lugs, and only then is the handle pushed down, which drives the probe into the valve and opens it. Pressing the handle first pushes the probe into an unlocked coupler, which on a pressurised keg blows it off and sprays beer. Done by bartenders (O*NET 35-3011.00; 711,140 US jobs in BLS OEWS May 2023), who change kegs on shift, and barbacks (35-9011.00, dining room and cafeteria attendants and bartender helpers, 483,390).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the counter top (z = 74.75 cm). Keg: a full sixtel (5.16 US gal, 26.3 kg) of which the top is modelled, standing loose and unclamped on the wet counter centred at x 28.0, y 0.0: a 23.0 cm stainless 12-sided top plate 1.2 cm up resting on a 2 mm tall, 8 mm wide 12-flat bottom chime ring at 10.5 cm radius (static and sliding friction 0.10, no hold-down or clamp), a 4 mm chime wall round its edge 4.0 cm tall, and in the middle the Sankey D valve neck, a 3.4 cm across-flats chrome octagon rising 1.6 cm above the plate (top 2.8 cm up, friction 0.10) with two dark bayonet lugs (1.0 x 0.3 x 0.6 cm) on opposite faces rotated 45 deg counter-clockwise from left-right (near-left and far-right). Drip tray: fixed black block 10.0 x 10.0 x 0.8 cm at x 28.0, y -20.0. Coupler: chrome Sankey D coupler, 0.90 kg in all (0.75 kg body, 0.10 kg handle, 0.05 kg probe), standing on the tray (seat face 1.4 cm up): a 6.4 cm square base with a 6 mm skirt (5.6 cm inside) that fits over the valve neck, orange bayonet ears (1.0 x 0.4 x 0.8 cm) on its left and right (y +-3.4 cm), a 4.6 cm square body 4.6 cm tall, a black beer outlet 1.6 cm square on top (2.5 cm tall) with an elbow turned down its far (+x) face (barb 4.6 cm above seat face), and a dark gas inlet (1.6 x 1.2 x 1.2 cm) on that face below it (barb 3.0 cm above seat face). Its handle (8.0 cm chrome bar with a black grip, 100 g) is pivoted on the body's near side (x -2.7 cm, z +4.4 cm above seat face), pointing toward the robot, raised 35 deg above horizontal; it turns down 60 deg to a stop on a 0.5 N m/rad spring that holds it up until horizontal (35 deg, over centre) and holds it down past horizontal. Inside, a dark probe (1.4 x 1.4 x 3.0 cm, 50 g) is cammed by the handle 11.5 mm down into the valve (full travel at 54 deg handle travel). Lines: both stay connected all episode. Beer line: 36 cm of 1.0 cm clear vinyl from the outlet elbow (6.0 cm up), starting at heading -60 deg and curving +18.0 deg per segment round the far side of the tray (out to y -26.1 cm) to x 44.87, y -8.52, z 6.0 cm at the shank of a fixed chrome tap tower (4.0 x 4.0 x 28.0 cm at x 42.94, y -6.78, yaw 138 deg). Gas line: 36 cm of 1.2 cm red hose from the gas inlet (4.4 cm up), starting at heading -50 deg and curving +15.5 deg per segment (out to y -25.2 cm) to x 50.04, y -7.18, z 4.4 cm at a fixed blue CO2 regulator (3.6 x 4.0 x 6.0 cm on a 2.0 x 2.0 cm dark post, yellow 1.0 x 3.0 x 1.2 cm shutoff lever on top closed at 0 psi, at x 48.82, y -5.11, yaw 120.5 deg). Each line is twelve 3.0 cm rigid segments of 20 g on alternating yaw, pitch and twist spring hinges (0.01 N m/rad, damping 0.002 N m s/rad, +-100 deg); each far end is welded to its fixture and breaks above 60 N. Their weight and stiffness act on the coupler throughout. Turning the coupler clockwise on the valve works against 0.92 N m bayonet lug and seal friction (acting equally on the free-standing keg) and 0.4 N m ramp draw-in over the last 15 deg to the 90 deg stop.
scoring: From the episode's recorded poses (trial video, ruler and protractor on a real rig). Caught: coupler seat within 11 mm horizontally and from 2 mm below to 3 mm above the valve seat on the moving keg, upright within 5 deg, and ears within 10 deg of the 45 deg lug-entry line. All subsequent turn angles are measured relative to the keg's valve, so spinning the keg with the coupler earns no turn; sliding or spinning the keg on the counter is not penalised. Score 0, latched for the episode, if the handle stays more than 30 deg down for 0.25 s while the coupler is turned less than 80 deg on the valve, if the keg tilts more than 20 deg or its base drops more than 20 mm below the counter, if the coupler is knocked over (tilted more than 30 deg) or its seat drops less than 10 mm above the counter, or if either hose's far end separates more than 5 mm from its fitting; also 0 if the coupler never caught. Otherwise the sum of: caught 0.1; turned 85 deg or more clockwise on the valve 0.25; handle locked over centre (52 deg or more down) 0.35; probe 90% or more of its 11.5 mm travel into the valve 0.2; turned 85 deg or more, neither gripper TCP within 2.0 cm of the coupler or handle bounding box, and coupler, handle and keg resting (linear speed below 0.01 m/s and angular speed below 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s 0.1. Success at 1.0 held for 1 s; otherwise scored at the last step.
reset_notes: Lift the handle back up past centre, turn the coupler back 90 deg and lift it off the valve, stand it on the drip tray with the handle pointing at the robot and both lines lying in their loops, check both line fittings are tight, and set the full keg back on its outline at (28, 0) cm with the lugs near-left and far-right (45 deg counter-clockwise from left-right), standing loose and unclamped on the wet counter (no clamp, strap, wedge or mat), with the CO2 regulator shutoff closed (0 psi).
fidelity: Rigid-box parts. Loose 26.3 kg keg cut to top 4 cm plus 2 mm chime ring (10.5 cm radius, friction 0.10; ~2.7 N m spin, ~26 N slide on wet steel; barrel CoM simplified). Bayonet is a coupler-keg revolute catch (collision on; 11 mm XY, -2..3 mm Z, 5 deg tilt, 10 deg yaw) with 0.92 N m trailing lug torque on both bodies and 0.4 N m draw-in (75-90 deg). Sprung handle and 11.5 mm probe. Two 12x3 cm, 20 g spring-hinged lines (60 N welds). Real rig: ballasted 26.3 kg keg, lines on, 0 psi.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (two runs, 854 steps); no-turn: 0.0; no-handle: 0.35; idle: 0.0
